entries.title: Each place has its own ways
entries.literal_meaning: Each place has its particular ways; each river has its bends.
entries.explanation: A way of doing things that feels ordinary in one place may differ elsewhere. The river image makes local variation easy to picture. The saying invites attention to the place you are in, without declaring every local practice beyond question.
entries.meaning_odia: ସବୁ ଅଞ୍ଚଳର ରୀତି ଏକା ପରି ନୁହେଁ। ନଈର ବାଙ୍କ ପରି ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ସ୍ଥାନର ନିଜସ୍ୱ ଢଙ୍ଗ ଅଛି। ନୂଆ ସ୍ଥାନର ଚଳଣି ବୁଝିବାକୁ ଏହି କଥା ମନେ ପକାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A visitor notices that a neighbouring village arranges its shared meal differently and asks how the local arrangement works. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The example appears under locality in the dictionary. A separate lexical entry gives particular and differing customs among the senses of ଫାଙ୍କ; that supports the reading used here.

entries.title: One hand cannot clap
entries.literal_meaning: A clap cannot sound with one hand alone.
entries.explanation: Some things require a response or a shared effort. The image of two palms meeting makes that dependence immediate. It can invite cooperation; it should not be used to assume that both sides bear equal blame for harm.
entries.meaning_odia: କିଛି କାମ ପାଇଁ ଉଭୟ ପକ୍ଷର ସହଯୋଗ ଦରକାର। ଗୋଟିଏ ପକ୍ଷର ଚେଷ୍ଟାରେ ସବୁବେଳେ କାମ ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ। ତେବେ କାହାରି କ୍ଷତି ହେଲେ ଉଭୟ ପକ୍ଷ ସମାନ ଦୋଷୀ ବୋଲି ଏଥିରୁ ଧରିନେବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: One person proposes a shared reading group; the others must also make time for it. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly labels this example a dhaga under clapping. The explanation here is editorial, not a recorded account of its first use.
